question: How many European countries will ECDC report with locally-acquired human West Nile virus cases in the 2026 season as of its mid-October weekly update?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: 16 countries as of the week 38 (17 Sep) and week 40 (30 Sep) ECDC updates, so the count has plateaued. Resolution is the first update on or after 15 Oct, which leaves about 2 weekly updates. In past seasons countries were occasionally added in October (Cyprus and Poland in 2024), but usually not once the count is flat. Main upside: Bulgarian media reported Bulgaria's first 2026 WNV case in the week of 17-23 Aug, yet Bulgaria is not on ECDC's list; it could appear late or may not qualify. Other candidates (Slovenia, Slovakia, Türkiye, Portugal) are possible as activity fades. The count cannot fall below 16 because cases are not removed. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Estimate: P(16)~0.70, P(17)~0.22, P(18+)~0.08.
calls.dossier:
- ECDC CDTR week 38 2026 (search snippet): as of 17 Sep 2026, 180 affected areas in 16 countries, 1,482 locally acquired cases. Countries: IT, EL, RO, FR, NL, RS, HR, ES, BE, MK, DE, HU, AT, XK, AL, CY.
- Question background: week 40 update (data to 30 Sep 2026) shows 1,765 cases, 202 areas, still the same 16 countries; 16 newly affected areas that week, mostly in countries already listed.
- Trajectory: 6-7 countries in early Aug; 12 around 21 Aug (RTE/MedicalXpress); 15 later (zdrave.net headline); 16 by 17 Sep; unchanged through 30 Sep.
- Bulgaria: marica.bg (2026, search snippet) reports NCIPD registered Bulgaria's first 2026 WNV case in reporting week 17-23 Aug. Bulgaria was still absent from the ECDC list as of 30 Sep. Not confirmed whether the case was locally acquired or why it is missing (reporting lag vs not meeting the case definition). The 24chasa 'fourth case' article is from 2024, not 2026.
- Countries with past local cases but none on the 2026 list: Bulgaria, Slovenia, Slovakia, Türkiye, Portugal, Czechia, Poland, Bosnia, Montenegro, Ukraine.
- Historical: Cyprus and Poland were added in October 2024, so additions this late do happen; whether a 2025 country was added in October was not verified.
- Mosticare page is stale (data to 5 Aug); ECDC dashboard wnv-weekly.ecdc.europa.eu refused connection; ECDC landing page reported 'last updated 10 September'.
- Resolves off the headline country count in the first ECDC weekly update on or after 15 Oct 2026 (expected Fri 16 Oct, data to about 14 Oct), not national bulletins. The count does not drop within a season.
- Event window: from now (5 Oct) to the update on or after 15 Oct; about 2 weekly updates remain (about 9 Oct and 16 Oct).
- Searched but not found: any report of a new country's first 2026 local case in late Sep/early Oct; a 2025 week 40 to week 42 comparison; any prediction market (none on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers).
calls.reference_class: ECDC WNV seasonal country counts: how many countries are added between the end-September update and the mid-October update, in seasons when the count was already flat

calls.reasoning: Count was 16 in the 17 Sep update and still 16 in the week 40 update (data to 30 Sep), so two weeks with no new country. Two more weekly updates (~9 and 16 Oct) remain before resolution. Reference class: country additions in ECDC WNV seasons during early-to-mid October. 2024 added Cyprus and Poland in October; 2025 rose from 13 countries (3 Oct) to 14 (29 Oct). Bulgaria and Türkiye reported cases in 2025 but are absent in 2026; Türkiye often reports late. Most likely outcome is the status quo of 16, with a meaningful chance of 17. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

A new country is plausible but not the default: in October 2024, Cyprus and Poland were added. Bulgaria reported a domestic first 2026 case in late August that ECDC has not listed (it may be imported or a reporting lag), which makes Bulgaria a concrete candidate. Türkiye, Slovenia and Slovakia are the other usual late reporters. Country counts essentially never drop. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers. calls.reasoning: Status quo is 16 countries, unchanged from the 17 Sep update through the Week 40 data (30 Sep). About two weekly updates remain before resolution (around 9 and 16 Oct) as the season wanes. October additions do happen (Cyprus and Poland in 2024; 2025 went from 13 to 14 in October), but most short windows add none. Bulgaria's August domestic case has gone unlisted by ECDC for about 6 weeks, which weakens it as a candidate. Türkiye, a late reporter, and Slovenia/Slovakia are the remaining upside. The count cannot fall. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: 16 countries as of 17 Sep and 30 Sep; two updates left; the count does not drop; Cyprus/Poland added Oct 2024; Bulgaria's August case is unlisted. Run 2 alone adds 2025 data (13 to 14 countries between 3 and 29 Oct). That is consistent with the others and only partly overlaps this year's window. The open factual question is whether Bulgaria's case was locally acquired; it cannot be settled without web access. Six weeks off the ECDC list argues against imminent inclusion, so it gets only moderate weight. The rest is judgment on how likely a late addition is. I carry forward the shared reading of P(16) about 0.72. My percentiles match the runs because the evidence puts me there, not because I averaged them.
